newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Stg choppy between 2.93 and 2.96 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Stg choppy between 2.93 and 2.96 marks.

text.p: Sterling/mark is set for another choppy trading session, with slightly corrective pressure dominating after its inability to challenge recent highs again, technical analysts said.
Monday's rollercoaster ride was held on the downside by firm support around the 2.9310 mark level. On the upside, sterling finds it hard, however, to reclaim territory above 2.96, analysts said.
"The decline to 2.9310 has added a bit of short-term vulnerability but we are still in a very powerful uptrend," said David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
At 0725 GMT the pound was at 2.9538/48 marks and $1.6839/49 compared with 2.9385/95 and $1.6845/55 in late Europe Monday.
Sneddon said the risk of a correction would increase below 2.9460, former key support, and a pivot line at 2.9360. "But at the moment everybody is still top-picking," he said.

A technical analyst at a UK bank said a move to major psychological resistance at 3.00 marks was still possible over the coming days but the pound faced strong resistance at 2.9620 ahead of an even firmer barrier at 2.9680.
"A sustained drop below the 2.9460 area would increase pressure on the downside," the analyst said.
Cable is likely to face a struggle at the $1.6900 level, which capped the pound on Monday, and is also an area of congestion dating back to January.

Chartists saw initial support at 1.6810, which was tested and held on Monday. A drop below would spark a double-top on the hourly charts and trigger a more pronounced pullback to 1.6700/20, the UK bank analyst said.
This area marks a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the pound's upmove this month from $1.6508 to a near seven-month high at $1.6929 and should provide firm support.
